chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Sa'id al-Azraq, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning
A man who killed a believing man, he said: "It will be said to him: Die whatever kind of death you wish—if you wish, as a Jew; if you wish, as a Christian; and if you wish, as a Magian."

key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man; the subject under discussion
key_terms.مَجُوسِيًّا: as a Magian; one of the condemned states mentioned in the wording
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer; the victim whose faith gives the crime special gravity
key_terms.مِيتَةٍ: a manner of death; the form or state in which one dies
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيًّا: as a Christian; one of the condemned states mentioned in the wording
key_terms.يَهُودِيًّا: as a Jew; one of the condemned states mentioned in the wording
key_terms.يُقَالُ: it will be said; a declaration addressed to the killer

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about the punishment of someone who kills a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith speaks with extreme severity about the one who kills a believing person, expressing the enormity of that crime. Its wording indicates grave moral and spiritual ruin for the killer and underscores the sanctity of the believer's life.
